# Why now

> Our table shows a warning that it changed since we published it. Do we have to publish it again, or is it still fine?
> — A colleague from SEO, a month after publishing

Search Console impressions, whole site has been at 3 · Confirmed for a month, and colleagues across the company build on it. Since then the Data Team added a field to it in dbt, and a colleague from marketing asked a Question on it. Nothing needs publishing again, but nothing looks after the Resource by itself either.

Promise: what staying the Owner of a published Resource asks of you: its changes, its Messages and its Level.

# Core idea

Publishing starts the work of an **Owner** rather than ending it: you mark changes seen, answer Messages, and act when its Level drops.

## At Immoscoop

The field the Data Team added shows as a warning on Search Console impressions, whole site, to everyone who sees it, with what changed and when, and SEO gets a Message; the Level stays 3 · Confirmed and nothing is published again. A colleague of SEO reads what the field holds, writes its Business Description, and marks the change seen: the warning goes. The Question from marketing, why the clicks are lower than in Search Console's own screen, they answer on the Resource, where the next colleague with the same Question reads it too; as it trips more people up, it goes on the card as a pitfall. Months later a run of dbt loses the description of the table: the Level drops to 1 · Available and SEO is told, while the Publication stays. They ask the Data Team to restore it, as a Business Description does not count towards the Level, and once it is back the Resource is 3 · Confirmed again: a Confirmation does not expire. Its next Level, 4 · Explored, comes later, with an EDA that covers at least its Key Fields.

# Check your understanding

## The Data Team renames a field of a Resource your Owner Unit published. What do you do?

- [ ] Publish it again, so that your Confirmation covers the new name
- [ ] Nothing: the Data Team made the change, so it is theirs to follow up
- [x] Read what changed, make the card say what colleagues need to know about it, and mark the change seen

Why: a change lowers no Level and asks for no new Confirmation, so nothing is published again; the warning stays for everyone who sees the Resource until it is marked seen. The Data Team knows how the field is built, you know what it means for the colleagues who read it.

## A colleague sends a Signal on a Resource your Owner Unit published: yesterday's figures look half of what they should be. Who answers it?

- [ ] The Data Team: a Signal is about the data, and the data is theirs
- [ ] Nobody: a Signal is a note for whoever reads the Resource next
- [x] Your Owner Unit as well as the Data Team: both get it, and you know what the figures mean, such as a source that completes its last days late

Why: a Signal goes to the Owner and to the Data Team. The Data Team looks at how the data is built; you know what it stands for, and whether the answer belongs on the card, where the next colleague reads it before sending the same Signal.

## A year after you published a Resource, nothing changed and nobody asked anything. What does it need from you?

- [ ] A new Confirmation: a Confirmation runs for a year
- [ ] To be published again, so that colleagues know it is still current
- [x] Nothing until a change, a Message or a drop of its Level comes in: a Confirmation does not expire

Why: there is no expiry date and no reminder. The Level drops only when what it stands on goes away, such as the descriptions in dbt, and Data Hub tells you when it does.

# You can now

keep a Resource you published worth relying on: mark its changes seen, answer its Messages on the Resource, and ask "what changed since we confirmed it?" when a warning or a drop of its Level comes in.
